newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:

Asked to react to the Egyptian import ban on live cattle from Portugal, France and Ireland, spokesman Gerard Kiely said the Commission found no justification for such a ban. He said the risk of BSE outside the UK was minimal since these countries' policy was to destroy the whole herd when a single case of BSE was found.

In answer to a question on new South Korean labour laws and the human rights clause in the EU-Korean agreement, spokesman Peter Guilford said the accord was at the ratification stage and that there had been no reaction at Commission level so far.
The Commission released the following documents:
- Speech/97/2: Speech by Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan on "Flexibility and enlargement, how UK can play its cards right".
- Remarks by the High Representative Mr Carl Bildt at the donors' information meeting.
- Bosnia and Herzegovina: The priority reconstruction program: from emergency to sustainability.
- Memo/97/2: The European Union and the French overseas territories.
